t.d: Miki smithing tradition of carpentry blades—saws, chisels, planes, knives and large construction tools.
t.tech: forge-welding carbon steel to iron with borax flux, forging, annealing in straw ash, water quench, two-stage tempering, polishing
t.auth: laminated hard-steel edge on softer iron; smith's stamp

t.d: Natural Japanese waterstones (tennen toishi) quarried for finishing blades, used wet.
t.tech: quarried and cut stone used with water

t.d: Slim French slip-joint pocket knife with a tapered blade and ornamented backspring.
t.tech: slip-joint assembly, forged or stamped blade
t.mat: cattle horn, wood, aluminium; stainless or carbon steel (XC75, XC100)
t.auth: 'Laguiole' is a generic name, not a protected one; French makers often stamp their mark and steel type on the blade.

t.d: Japanese tool-making town where the higonokami friction folder is still made.
t.tech: folded sheet-metal handle, flat-ground laminated blade
t.auth: handle stamped with maker's name and blade steel

t.d: Savoie folding knives made by Opinel in numbered sizes, with the Virobloc collar from 1955.
t.mat: beech and other woods; carbon or stainless steel
t.auth: numbered blade size and Opinel logo stamped on the blade.

t.d: Sheffield has been famous for cutlery since the 17th century; crucible and stainless steel pioneered there, with remaining 'little mester' workshops.
t.tech: forging and grinding, crucible steel, stainless steel
t.mat: carbon and stainless steel, bone, horn and wood scales
t.auth: 'Made in Sheffield' mark and Cutlers' Company registered marks; vintage carvers often bear maker and 'Sheffield England'

t.d: The 'Klingenstadt' tradition of forged swords, knives, scissors and razors behind Wüsthof, Zwilling, Böker, Güde and Herder.
t.tech: drop-forging from a single blank with integral bolster, ice-hardening, hand finishing
t.mat: X50CrMoV15 stainless, carbon steels, POM and wood handles
t.auth: 'Solingen' is a protected origin mark; forged full tang, maker's trident/twins stamps

t.d: Swedish forges making hand-forged axes, each signed by its smith.
t.auth: smith's initials stamped on each head

t.d: France's knife capital on the Durolle river, source of most French cutting tools including laguiole-type and steak knives.
t.tech: forged blades; hand assembly and fitting of handles; polishing
t.mat: stainless and carbon steel, horn, wood, resin
t.auth: Le Thiers model (1993) is a registered town pattern; 'laguiole' alone is not a protected name, so check for a maker's stamp.
